board-minutes-of-meeting.0: Board minutes of meeting are not ordinary meeting notes. Indian company law treats properly kept minutes as evidence of what the board decided, and they get checked in audits, due diligence and disputes. One missing resolution or unsigned page can create real problems years later.
board-minutes-of-meeting.1: Inside: the legal rules, a copy-ready format and sample for a private limited company, and the mistakes company secretaries see most often.
board-minutes-of-meeting.3: General meeting minutes record meetings of shareholders, while committee minutes record meetings of board committees such as the audit committee. Board minutes are different from both.
board-minutes-of-meeting.5: Who signs? The chairperson of that meeting, or the chairperson of the next meeting. Since 1 April 2024 the revised SS-1 has applied, so check you are using the current version.
board-minutes-of-meeting.6: Drawn from SS-1 practice, these items should go into board minutes of meeting in India:
board-minutes-of-meeting.9: Keep the discussion summary short and the resolution text exact. Why? Banks, auditors and registrars will ask for the resolution.
board-minutes-of-meeting.11: A company must hold its first board meeting within 30 days of incorporation and at least 4 board meetings a year, with no more than 120 days between 2 consecutive meetings, under [Section 173](https://lawx.in/acts/section/24/314/3020). One person companies (other than those with a single director), small companies and dormant companies need at least 1 meeting in each half of the calendar year, at least 90 days apart (Section 173(5)).
board-minutes-of-meeting.12: At least 7 days' written notice must go to directors. Quorum, under Section 174(1), is one-third of the total strength of the board or 2 directors, whichever is higher, and directors joining by video conferencing count toward it. Each meeting needs its own minutes.
board-minutes-of-meeting.13: Board minutes are not a contract. They are evidence, though. Minutes kept in line with the Act are evidence of the proceedings recorded (Section 118(7)). Section 118(8) adds that, until the contrary is proved, the meeting is deemed duly called and held, and appointments of directors, key managerial personnel and auditors recorded in the minutes are deemed valid.
board-minutes-of-meeting.14: That is why accuracy matters. Once signed, minutes should not be altered under SS-1 practice; any correction should be approved at a later meeting and recorded in that meeting's minutes.
board-minutes-of-meeting.15: Yes. Indian companies can hold board meetings through video conferencing or other audio-visual means, subject to the rules and certain restricted matters. Minutes must record which directors attended this way, and the chairperson must confirm attendance and quorum.
board-minutes-of-meeting.16: A recording helps the company secretary draft accurate minutes. Still, the minutes remain the legal record. Not the recording.
board-minutes-of-meeting.19: Need general meeting minutes outside the board? See our [minutes of meeting format](https://lynkk.ai/blog/minutes-of-meeting-format) and the difference between [meeting notes and minutes](https://lynkk.ai/blog/meeting-notes-vs-minutes).
board-minutes-of-meeting.20: SS-1 sets 15 days for draft minutes to reach directors and 7 days for their comments. Section 118 requires minutes to be prepared, signed and kept within 30 days. A certified copy of the signed minutes goes to directors within 15 days of signing.
board-minutes-of-meeting.21: The chairperson of the meeting signs the minutes, or the chairperson of the next meeting if needed. Usually the company secretary prepares them. Each meeting's minutes end with a dated, signed last page. Directors receive a certified copy of the signed minutes, so everyone works from the same final record.
board-minutes-of-meeting.22: Board and committee meeting minutes must be preserved permanently, usually in the minutes book kept at the company's registered office. Keep supporting papers, such as notices and board packs, alongside them. Why? Auditors and due diligence teams usually ask for both together.
board-minutes-of-meeting.24: Board minutes are internal records. They are not public filings, but they may be inspected by directors, auditors and authorities, and some resolutions must be filed with the Registrar of Companies. Directors should treat them as confidential unless the board decides otherwise.
